messages:
jessica_support: raising an escalation — customer ACME reporting sporadic 502s from the hosted inference endpoint since ~09:23 UTC. They see SSL handshake timeouts and gateway errors. sample logs from their side attached below. asking for an on-call triage.

jessica_support: logs from customer (redacted):

```
POST /v1/generate 502 Gateway Error
error: TLS handshake timeout after 10s
remote: tls handshake failed: EOF
request_id: req_3b9a2f
```

mike_oncall_sre: on it. do we have our request IDs for those requests? any matching req ids on edge? also what region is the traffic from?

jessica_support: customer provided their req id above (req_3b9a2f). region eu-west-1. also sees spikes in client-side latency ~3s before 502. I've attached their PCAP snippet.

anya_eng_runtime: curious if this is an edge resolver issue or cert rotation ripple. did we rotate certs recently for eu-west-1?

resolver-bot: automated notice: scheduled dns-rotation job executed at 2026-02-26T09:15:12Z for eu-west-1. 3 resolver endpoints cycled. observed increased servfail rate to a subset of authoritative nameservers for ~80s.

mike_oncall_sre: that matches timeline. jessica, can you paste one failing curl from the customer? want the TLS handshake details.

jessica_support: they ran:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate
*   Trying 198.51.100.24:443...
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.example (198.51.100.24) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection attempt timed out after 10000 ms
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake timeout
```

mike_oncall_sre: can anyone run a dig +trace from an eu-west probe for api.redwood-inference.example and paste results? i want to check if glue/a records were transiently inconsistent.

anya_eng_runtime: from our eu-west health probe (09:20-09:40):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.redwood-inference.example @1.1.1.1
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.example. 60 IN A 198.51.100.24
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
example. 300 IN NS ns1.example.
;; SERVER: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)
;; Query time: 520 msec
```

anya_eng_runtime: note the Query time spikes to ~500ms and occasional SERVFAILs for the authoritative chain between 09:15:10-09:16:40. looks like upstream authoritative nameserver had a partition while resolver rotation happened.

mike_oncall_sre: thanks. that pattern can lead to clients attempting a TCP connect to the edge but then waiting on TLS handshake because the edge couldn't obtain updated cert chain or the client got a stale A record that pointed at a host mid-rotation. i want the edge logs for req_3b9a2f — jessica, can you escalate logs from edge eu-west-1 for 09:20-09:26?

jessica_support: attached edge logs:
```
[09:23:12] req_3b9a2f accepted from 198.51.100.130
[09:23:12] upstream connect 198.51.100.24:443 success
[09:23:22] tls: handshake timeout for connection id 0x7f3ab2
[09:23:22] req_3b9a2f -> 502 gateway_error handshake_timeout
```

anya_eng_runtime: those tls timeouts on the edge are consistent with either transient network loss to the node performing the cert handshake, or the cert chain retrieval got delayed by resolver flakiness if we fetch A/CAA/OCSP during handshake. do we have OCSP stapling enabled for that cert?

mike_oncall_sre: yes, OCSP stapling enabled. if the OCSP responder had higher latency while resolvers were flapping, the handshake could stall waiting for stapling. i want to check our OCSP probe metrics.

resolver-bot: OCSP probe alert: increased latency to ocsp.example-ca.com between 09:14:30-09:17:00 by ~4s for eu-west-1.

mike_oncall_sre: ok, root cause is lining up: dns rotation caused resolver timeouts which cascaded into OCSP and cert validation delays causing TLS handshakes to exceed our handshake timeout and return 502s to customers.

sam_cust_success: jumped in with customer: informed ACME that we are investigating; they reported ~12 failed requests over a 4min window and are seeing app retries. offered to escalate and provide mitigations.

anya_eng_runtime: mitigation plan: 1) add temporary DNS override in node hosts cache for the affected edge node to skip external resolver for critical cert/ocsp hostnames, 2) increase local OCSP timeout fallback and cache stapling for 5m, 3) roll back the resolver rotation job if it is still in progress.

mike_oncall_sre: doing 1 and 2 now. applying a short-lived override via our config manager to pin ocsp.example-ca.com -> 203.0.113.10 on eu-west edge hosts, and bump ocsp fallback timeout to 10s. will also purge DNS negative cache to force re-resolve.

deploy-bot: config change applied: dns_override ocsp.example-ca.com -> 203.0.113.10 on 6 hosts in eu-west-1 at 09:32:10Z. config_id cfg_9921.

mike_oncall_sre: restarted edge workers to pick up overrides and cleared DNS cache. starting a canary test.

anya_eng_runtime: i see handshake success rates climb after 09:33. canary looks good.

jessica_support: customer confirmation: ACME reports errors stopped after ~09:35 and they see normal traffic resumed. they want root cause and ETA on permanent fix.

mike_oncall_sre: immediate cause: transient authoritative nameserver partition + resolver rotation coinciding with OCSP latency spike. short-term mitigation we applied: dns override + increased OCSP fallback cache.

anya_eng_runtime: long-term fixes: 1) make resolver-rotation job stagger resilient to in-flight authoritative flakiness, 2) add local OCSP stapling cache with longer TTLs to avoid blocking handshakes during short DNS flaps, 3) add circuit-breaker to fallback to secondary resolvers quicker, 4) add observability to correlate resolver rotation with handshake failures.

sam_cust_success: shared summary with ACME and offered a postmortem once done. they asked for a timeline — proposing a week for rolling the OCSP cache change and 2 weeks to update resolver-rotation logic.

mike_oncall_sre: action items assigned:
- anya_eng_runtime: design OCSP local cache and fallback behavior (due EOD +7)
- eng-infra (ticket INF-4502): add safer stagger to resolver rotation job (due +14d)
- obs-team: dashboard correlating resolver job runs, DNS SERVFAILs, and TLS handshake timeouts (due +3d)

jessica_support: closing loop with customer and scheduling postmortem. will attach logs and timeline. thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike_oncall_sre: follow-up note: no evidence of certificate mis-issuance or private key problems — purely availability and timing cascade. marking incident as resolved for now.

resolver-bot: cleanup task scheduled: remove temporary dns_override cfg_9921 at 2026-02-26T12:00:00Z unless flagged.
